title: James River Recruits Georgia Collier and Matt Sinosky, Completing E&S Leadership Reorganization
summary: PEMBROKE, Bermuda, Oct. 06, 2025 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- James River Group Holdings, Ltd. ("James River" or the "Company") (NASDAQ: JRVR) today announced the appointments of Georgia Collier and Matt Sinosky to its Excess and Surplus (“E&S”) leadership team, each reporting to Todd Sutherland , President
body_text: PEMBROKE, Bermuda, Oct. 06, 2025 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- James River Group Holdings, Ltd. ("James River" or the "Company") (NASDAQ: JRVR) today announced the appointments of Georgia Collier and Matt Sinosky to its Excess and Surplus (“E&S”) leadership team, each reporting to Todd Sutherland, President of E&S. These two appointments support James River’s continued momentum to capture market opportunities and drive its next phase of profitable growth. With more than two decades of experience in the E&S market, Georgia Collier re-joins James River from the Markel Group where she led the firm’s nationwide Commercial Primary Casualty division as a Managing Director and Product Line Leader. She previously spent nearly 20 years at James River overseeing various underwriting units during her tenure. Ms. Collier will work from the Company’s Richmond office. In her new role, and a newly created role for the Company, as Senior Vice President, Collier will lead the segment’s Specialty underwriting division. She will oversee all facets of planning and executive leadership of Specialty’s six underlying underwriting sub-divisions (Allied Health, Energy, Environmental, Life Sciences, Management Liability, and Professional Liability) to maximize profitable growth and further establish the Company as a valued partner to brokers in each of these unique lines of business. Matt Sinosky joins James River from Arch Capital Group Ltd where he served as Vice President of Wholesale Distribution and led wholesale efforts across six business units within Arch Insurance Group. He has spent over fifteen years in the insurance distribution landscape, focused on engaging the wholesale distribution channel. As the Vice President of Business Development & Distribution, Mr. Sinosky will lead the Company’s dedicated wholesale channel efforts, partnering with wholesale brokers and overseeing marketing and distribution strategies to strengthen the Company’s competitive position and deliver strategic growth. Todd Sutherland, President of E&S commented, “I am excited to welcome two dynamic industry leaders to James River that will complement our existing team and increase our ability to win for our clients. Georgia and Matt have led critical functions within our market for years, bringing a track record of portfolio management, underwriting experience and deep industry relationships within the small-medium enterprise sector.” Frank D’Orazio, CEO commented, “The addition of these two executives underscores the market opportunity ahead and reflect James River’s continued ability to attract top-tier industry talent. We are confident they will add great value to our E&S team.” Forward Looking Statements This press release contains forward-looking statements as that term is defined in the Private Securities Litigation Reform Act of 1995. About James River Group Holdings, Ltd. James River Group Holdings, Ltd. is a Bermuda-based insurance holding company that owns and operates a group of specialty insurance companies. The Company operates in two specialty property-casualty insurance segments: Excess and Surplus Lines and Specialty Admitted Insurance. Each of the Company’s regulated insurance subsidiaries are rated “A-” (Excellent) by A.M. Best Company. Visit James River Group Holdings, Ltd. on the web at www.jrvrgroup.com . title: Mehr Motivation im SHK-Betrieb: 5 sofort wirksame Maßnahmen für Ihre Mitarbeiter
summary: Mehr Motivation im SHK-Betrieb: 5 sofort wirksame Maßnahmen für Ihre Mitarbeiter – Praxistipps für SHK- und Haustechnik-Betriebe im Hey Telo Blog.
body_text: Motivierte Mitarbeiter sind das Rückgrat jedes SHK-Betriebs. Gerade in Zeiten von Fachkräftemangel und hohem Auftragsvolumen entscheidet die Stimmung im Team über Qualität, Kundenzufriedenheit und langfristige Bindung. Als Geschäftsführer haben Sie direkten Einfluss darauf, wie motiviert Ihr Team täglich ans Werk geht. 1 | Klare Kommunikation statt Flurfunk Transparenz schafft Vertrauen. Halten Sie Ihr Team regelmäßig über Auftragslage, Ziele und Herausforderungen auf dem Laufenden – z. B. mit kurzen Wochen-Updates. So fühlt sich jeder eingebunden und weiß, warum sein Einsatz wichtig ist. 2 | Anerkennung sofort zeigen Ein „Danke“ nach erfolgreichem Kundenauftrag wirkt stärker als eine jährliche Ansprache. Nutzen Sie kleine Gesten: loben Sie gute Arbeit im Teamchat oder hängen Sie ein „Auftrags-Champion der Woche“-Board in der Werkstatt aus. 3 | Weiterbildung als Wertschätzung Bieten Sie praxisnahe Schulungen an – etwa zu neuen Heiztechnologien oder digitalen Werkzeugen. Studien zeigen: Mitarbeiter, die sich weiterentwickeln können, bleiben bis zu 40 % länger im Betrieb. Praxis-Hack: Auch ein einstündiges Kurz-Webinar mit Herstellern motiviert enorm. 4 | Flexible Anreize schaffen Nicht jeder Mitarbeiter reagiert gleich. Während der eine eine kleine Prämie schätzt, freut sich der andere über einen halben freien Tag. Machen Sie Bonusmodelle variabel, um individuelle Bedürfnisse zu berücksichtigen. 5 | Moderne Tools zur Entlastung nutzen Weniger Stress bedeutet mehr Motivation. Digitale Helfer wie HeyTelo nehmen Telefonate und Terminorganisation ab, sodass Monteure und Büromitarbeiter sich auf ihre eigentliche Arbeit konzentrieren können – ohne Unterbrechungen und Überstunden. Fazit Motivation entsteht nicht durch große Reden, sondern durch konsequente, kleine Schritte im Alltag. Wer als Geschäftsführer Kommunikation verbessert, Anerkennung zeigt und sein Team mit den richtigen Werkzeugen entlastet, steigert nicht nur die Zufriedenheit, sondern auch Leistung und Kundenbindung. Starten Sie heute mit einem der Tipps – Ihr Team wird es Ihnen danken.

title: Artesian Reports Third Quarter and Year-To-Date 2025 Results
summary: Newark, Delaware, October 30, 2025 – Artesian Resources Corporation (Nasdaq: ARTNA), a leading provider on the Delmarva Peninsula of water...
body_text: Newark, Delaware, October 30, 2025 – Artesian Resources Corporation (Nasdaq: ARTNA), a leading provider on the Delmarva Peninsula of water and wastewater services, and a number of other related business services, today announced third quarter and year-to-date results for 2025. Diluted net income per share increased to $0.68 in the third quarter and $1.81 year-to-date Net income increased $0.1 million (2.2%) in the third quarter and $2.1 million (12.9%) year-to-date Invested $40.5 million year-to-date in water and wastewater infrastructure Third Quarter Results Net income for the three months ended September 30, 2025 was $7.0 million, a $0.1 million, or 2.2%, increase compared to net income for the three months ended September 30, 2024. Diluted net income per share increased 3.0% to $0.68, compared to $0.66 for the same period in 2024. Revenues totaled $30.5 million for the three months ended September 30, 2025, $1.3 million, or 4.6%, more than revenues for the three months ended September 30, 2024. Water sales revenue increased $0.7 million, or 3.1%, primarily the result of a temporary rate increase placed into effect on June 3, 2025, as permitted under Delaware law, until permanent rates are determined by the Delaware Public Service Commission, or DEPSC, as well as an increase in the number of customers served, partially offset by a slight decrease in consumption. Other utility operating revenue increased approximately $0.4 million, or 12.6%, primarily due to an increase in wastewater revenue associated with additional customers served. Non-utility operating revenue increased approximately $0.2 million, or 10.8%, primarily due to an increase in Service Line Protection Plan, or SLP Plan, revenue, resulting from an increase in rates placed into effect on December 1, 2024. summary: Tired of slow business onboarding? The average 5 back-and-forth interactions lead to customer drop-off. See how Arva AI's realtime analysis is making the process 100x quicker.
body_text: For any bank or fintech, the business onboarding process is the first, most critical handshake with a new customer. Unfortunately, for most, it’s a painfully slow and broken one. Consider the typical workflow: a new business customer signs up, fills out a form, and uploads their documents. Days later, a compliance analyst reviews the file, finds an error—a blurry document, a mistyped registration number, a missing UBO—and sends an email. The customer replies. The analyst reviews it again. This "5-step shuffle" is a familiar pain. On average, banks and fintechs face five back-and-forth interactions with their business customers just to get onboarding right. The True Cost of Friction This isn't just an operational inconvenience; it's a direct hit to your bottom line. Fatal Delays: The process is plagued by delays of days, and even weeks . Customer Drop-Off: In a competitive market, no one waits. A significant proportion of potential customers, frustrated by the friction, simply drop off and go to a competitor . Wasted Resources: Your highly-skilled compliance team is forced to spend its time chasing paperwork instead of focusing on high-risk decisions. The "What If" is Now What if there was a better way? Imagine an intelligent onboarding assistant that could interact with your customers in real-time . An assistant that guides them through the process, instantly spots that a document is for the wrong entity, and immediately asks them for the correct information—all in the same session. This is exactly what Arva AI enables. Banks and fintechs are now using Arva AI to completely streamline their onboarding process, making it up to 100x quicker . The key is eliminating the human review loop for simple, fixable errors. Realtime Analysis. Realtime Communication. Stronger Compliance. Arva’s API-first platform provides instant, automated feedback to your customers as they onboard. This is powered by a suite of realtime verification tools: Realtime Document Analysis: The moment a customer uploads a document, Arva’s AI analyzes it for legibility, validity, and consistency. No more waiting two days to find out a document was expired. Realtime Web Presence Analysis: Our AI instantly verifies the business's digital footprint, corroborating data from registries, company websites, and other sources to ensure the business is legitimate and operational. Realtime Communication: If an error is detected, Arva’s platform (via our API) communicates with the customer in that session , guiding them to fix the error on the spot. The result is a frictionless, one-shot onboarding experience for the customer. For the compliance team, it means the data they receive is correct, verified, and complete from the very beginning. It’s time to transform business verification for the better.
